subject: ela
intro: A collaborative conversation is a discussion where everyone follows rules to make the conversation fair and productive. Good conversation rules in Grade 1 include: listening carefully when someone else talks, speaking one at a time (not talking over each other), asking questions when you are confused, and building on what others say by connecting your ideas to theirs. These skills help students have better discussions about books, topics, and ideas.

items.prompt:
Read this conversation:
Tom: 'I think the best animal is a dog.'
Mia: 'I agree! I have a dog too. She is very friendly.'
Tom: 'What is her name?'
Mia: 'Her name is Biscuit.'

What conversation rule is Tom following when he asks 'What is her name?'

steps: Tom is asking a question to learn more about what Mia said.
This follows the rule: 'ask questions to clear up confusion or learn more.'
Tom is also building on Mia's comment — he listened and responded to her specific detail.
solution.answer: Tom is following the rule of asking questions and building on what his partner said.

items.prompt:
Look at this conversation:
Alex: 'My favorite book is—'
Jordan: (interrupts) 'I like pizza! Can we talk about lunch?'

What conversation rule did Jordan break?

steps: Jordan interrupted Alex before he could finish his sentence.
Rule broken: Speak one at a time. Do not interrupt others.
Jordan also changed the topic entirely, which does not build on what Alex said.
Good conversationalists wait for their turn and stay on topic.
solution.answer: Jordan broke the rule of speaking one at a time and staying on topic.

items.prompt: How does 'building on what someone else says' look in a conversation? Give an example.

steps: Building on someone's comment means connecting your idea to what they just said.
Example: Maya says, 'I like the part where the bear woke up.' Kai responds, 'Yes, and I also liked when the bear found the honey — it was exciting!'
Kai used 'yes, and' to connect his idea to Maya's, moving the conversation forward.
The opposite — ignoring what was said and starting a new topic — does not build on others.
solution.answer: Building on others' talk means responding to what they said and adding a connected idea.

items.prompt:
A student does not understand what her partner said about the book. What should she do?
A) Stay silent and pretend she understood.
B) Ask a question to clear up her confusion.

steps: Standard 1.SL.A.1c says students should ask questions to clear up confusion about topics under discussion.
Staying silent when confused does not help the student learn.
Asking a question is the correct behavior — for example: 'Can you explain what you meant by that?'
solution.answer: B) She should ask a question to clear up her confusion.

items.prompt: During a class discussion, two students both want to speak at the same time. What is the correct thing for BOTH of them to do?

steps: Only one person should speak at a time.
Both students should respect that rule.
One student should pause and let the other finish before speaking.
A student can politely gain the floor by waiting, raising a hand, or saying 'May I add something?'
solution.answer: Both students should not speak at the same time. One should pause and wait for the other to finish, then take their turn respectfully.

items.prompt:
Read the conversation:
Lila: 'I think frogs are interesting.'
Omar: 'Me too! I learned that frogs can jump very far.'
Lila: 'Really? How far can they jump?'

Is this a good conversation? Which rules are being followed?
items.hint: Look for: listening, building on others' ideas, asking questions.

steps: Omar builds on Lila's idea — he agrees and adds a new fact.
Lila responds to Omar's fact with a follow-up question.
Both speakers listen and connect their comments to what was just said.
This is a great example of collaborative conversation.
solution.answer: Yes, this is a good conversation. Both students listen, build on each other's ideas, and ask questions.

items.prompt:
Which student is following good conversation rules?
A) Sam, who talks the whole time and never lets his partner speak.
B) Ana, who listens to her partner, waits for a pause, and then shares her idea.
items.hint: Good conversations include listening and taking turns.

steps: Sam is monopolizing the conversation — his partner cannot contribute.
Ana is listening and waiting for her turn — this is the correct behavior.
Good conversations involve equal participation, not one person dominating.
solution.answer: B) Ana is following good conversation rules.

items.prompt:
After a teacher reads a story, a student says: 'I liked the story. The rabbit was funny.' Her partner says: 'I liked it too! The rabbit made me laugh when he fell in the mud.' Is the partner building on the first student's comment?
A) Yes
B) No
items.hint: Does the partner respond to what was said, or start a completely different topic?

steps: The partner agrees ('I liked it too!') and adds a specific detail that relates to the first student's comment about the rabbit.
This is building on what was said — the conversation stays on topic and gets more specific.
solution.answer: A) Yes, the partner is building on the first student's comment.

items.prompt:
A student is confused about what a classmate said during a discussion. What should she say?
A) Nothing — she does not want to seem confused.
B) 'Can you tell me more about what you mean?'
items.hint: Think about asking questions to clear up confusion.

steps: Asking for clarification is a key conversation skill (1.SL.A.1c).
Option B is polite and direct — it asks for more information without being rude.
Option A (staying silent) leaves the confusion unresolved.
solution.answer: B) She should ask, 'Can you tell me more about what you mean?'

items.prompt:
Here is a conversation about favorite books:
Kai: 'I love books about space.'
Nia: 'I like books about animals. Rainbows are pretty.'

What does Nia do wrong? What should she say instead?
items.hint: Check if Nia's comment connects to Kai's topic or goes somewhere completely different.

steps: Nia starts with a connected idea ('I like books about animals') but then adds 'Rainbows are pretty,' which is off-topic.
Going off-topic disrupts the conversation and does not build on what Kai said.
Better response: 'I like books about animals. Have you read any books about animals in space?'
solution.answer: Nia adds an off-topic comment ('Rainbows are pretty'). She should stay on the topic of favorite books.
